# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1–13 (Complete – Updated 107)

## Setting and Time
- **Current Period**: Spring of fourth year in Mirecombe hill farms (Seena with aching back; Ellan Lindner humming childhood tune while scrubbing step; Maric counting coins twice, coming up penny short; son Isnar Brackwood born to Wevie Lindner and Madan Brackwood, living in Mirecombe). Earlier: Winter of third year with frost on hedges. Even earlier: Evening at Brighton following Dobbin's arrival; fine brilliant moonlight night of May, warm and balmy. Army ordered to Belgium before week's end; mobilization imminent from Chatham. Three weeks before French Emperor likely attacks.
- **Primary Locations**: London (Russell Square, Thames Street counting-house, Slaughters' hotel, Gray's Inn Square, Cavendish Square fine hotel, Hulker and Bullock bankers on Lombard Street), Brighton (George-Amelia honeymoon, Rawdon-Rebecca residence, Ship Inn, bathing machines on beach), Mirecombe (Seena Orlwood—drowned in flood; Pebin Wexwood, Maric Lindson, Rozek Hollwood, Halan Hollwood, Isbin Hollwood, Orvie, Nynelle Stenworth, Seena Hollett, Brenelle and Orvie Hollett, Thidrek Corrett, Feten Lindner, children of Quenwick, Old Maric, Ilena Orlwood, Orrine, Staveton, Ellan Lindner, Wevie Lindner, Isnar Brackwood), Coldcombe hill farms, Dunholt village (Daric Brackwood, Thivie, Feena Stenworth, Cotho Brackwood, daughter Dalde Brackwood born), Chatham (embarkation point, inn with sitting-room prepared for travellers), Harwich (shipping departure point), Fulham (Mrs. Sedley's house, Mr. and Mrs. Clapp, Irish servant Miss Flannigan, Mr. Clapp gardening), Belgium (destination), Ghent, Brussels (military balls planned, Margate packets sailing daily)

## Main Characters

**Captain William Dobbin** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- **Brighton and London Actions - COMPLETED**: Arrived via Slaughters' hotel; witnessed Ensign Stubble's tears; dined with officers at theatre box. At Ship Inn: assumed "jovial and rattling manner" hiding feelings upon seeing Amelia; made clumsy compliments. In George's room: delivered lawyer's letter of disinheritance; George erupted blaming Dobbin; Dobbin offered personal financial support, promised not to forget godson in will; George forgave him. Evening dinner: assumed character of "rattle"; described Belgium fetes and fashion; when Rebecca announced intention to go to Belgium on staff, Dobbin flushed red, objected about danger, became "very confused and silent."
- **Cavendish Square Hotel - COMPLETED**: Attempted to remonstrate after dinner against extravagance of turtle and champagne for archbishop; George dismissed concerns. Dobbin walked home to Slaughters' musing about being in hackney-coach with Mrs. Osborne.
- **Chatham Arrival - CURRENT**: At Chatham inn, wearing shells on frockcoat, crimson sash and sabre; has been pacing street for an hour past in expectation of friends' arrival; presents military appearance that made Jos proud to claim his acquaintance.
- **Internal Conflict**: Deeply troubled by guilt over hastening marriage; feels his own unendurable suspense drove him to crush uncertainty; considers himself traitor to both father and son. Secret adoration of Amelia is now his "greatest privilege and hope of life"; privately resolved he would not have let her go to Belgium if married to her; will not remonstrate with George as master. Knows Amelia considers him plain, awkward, ungainly; acquiesces humbly; acknowledges "a time came when she knew him better" but that was distant.
- **Reputation**: "Greatly respected in the regiment, as the best officer and the cleverest man in it"
- **Piano Purchase**: Bought piano for Amelia's father's house at Fulham

**George Osborne** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- **Status - MARRIED, DISINHERITED**: Married Amelia late April without father's consent; honeymoon at Brighton; disinherited by father's lawyer letter (determination "final and irrevocable"). Receives £2,000 in 4 percent annuities and £100/year widow's allowance for Amelia.
- **Financial Crisis - ACUTE**: Lost £140 to Rawdon Crawley at cards; gave substantial payment to Rawdon from bank-notes and bill on agents. Hotel bill and card losses "almost drained the young man's purse."
- **Lawyer Visit - COMPLETED**: Upon arrival in London, wrote to father's solicitors requesting interview. Appeared before Mr. Higgs (attorney) expecting compromise message; met with "chilling coolness and indifference"; Higgs calculated £2,000 stock at rate of day; offered choice of cheque or purchased stock. George demanded cheque with "Damn the shillings and halfpence, sir," flattering himself he had put the old quiz to blush; stalked out with paper in pocket.
- **Banking - COMPLETED**: Proceeded to Hulker and Bullock bankers on Lombard Street; received his money; gloated over sum, never having had such amount before. Frederick Bullock (cadaverous suitor of George's sister Jane) was present; upon seeing Captain, his yellow face turned deadly colour and he slunk guiltily into inmost parlour. George too busy gloating to mark his countenance or flight.
- **Expectations**: Believes father will relent before long. Determines that if personal merits fail, he will distinguish himself prodigiously in ensuing campaign so old gentleman must give in. Reflects "the world was before him" and luck might change at cards; calculates "a deal of spending in two thousand pounds."
- **Current Status - CHATHAM**: Sent Amelia once more in carriage to her mother with strict orders and carte blanche to purchase everything requisite for lady of Mrs. George Osborne's fashion going on foreign tour. Paid Amelia's purchases with cheques on his agents "with the splendour of a lord." At Chatham inn; highly pleased with his day's business. Received triangular billet on pink paper from Mrs. Major O'Dowd addressed to Mrs. Captain Osborne, sealed with dove and olive branch in light blue sealing wax, written in large undecided female hand. George recognized "Peggy O'Dowd's fist" by kisses on seal. Directed Amelia must attend small friendly party that very evening; said she must make acquaintance with regiment there. Noted O'Dowd goes in command of regiment, "and Peggy goes in command."

**Amelia Osborne** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- **Emotional Crisis - RESOLVED**: Initially troubled by Rebecca's wit and accomplishments; misgives about Rebecca; observed George suffering ennui; tormented by guilt about forcing marriage and causing disinheritance. Face cleared reading disinheritance letter; idea of sharing poverty with beloved pleasant.
- **Resolution to Go to Belgium - EXECUTED**: Cried with "greatest spirit" determination to accompany George. Rose early morning; packed little trunks with "greatest alacrity" while George lay in bed.
- **Fulham Visit - COMPLETED**: Made "little disappointed curtsey" when George declined accompanying her. Went sadly down great staircase; Dobbin handed her into hackney-coach. Mother Mrs. Sedley clasped her to heart with "all maternal eagerness and affection," ran out of door weeping; old Mr. Clapp shrank back alarmed in shirt-sleeves; Irish servant-lass rushed up smiling "God bless you"; Amelia could hardly walk along flags.
- **Evening at Fulham - COMPLETED, MOOD TRANSFORMED**: Went upstairs to little room occupied before marriage; sank into chair; fell to thinking over past week; reflected on Rebecca's "twinkling green eyes and baleful smile"; indulged in usual mood of selfish brooding and listless melancholy; thought with terror of great funereal damask pavilion awaiting her at grand hotel; knelt by bedside seeking spiritual consolation. However, when tea was announced, came downstairs "a great deal more cheerful"; did not despond or deplore fate or think about George's coldness or Rebecca's eyes as she had been wont to do. Kissed father and mother; talked to old gentleman making him more merry than he had been for many a day. Sate down at piano (purchased by Dobbin) and sang all her father's favourite old songs. Pronounced tea excellent and praised exquisite taste in which marmalade was arranged in saucers. In determining to make everybody else happy, found herself so; was sound asleep in funereal pavilion; woke up with smile when George arrived from theatre.
- **Shopping Expedition - COMPLETED**: Sent by George once more in carriage to her mother with strict orders and carte blanche to purchase everything requisite for lady of Mrs. George Osborne's fashion going on foreign tour. Had but one day to complete outfit. Bustling about from milliner to linen-draper, escorted back to carriage by obsequious shopmen or polite owners. Mrs. Sedley was herself again almost, sincerely happy for first time since misfortunes. Amelia not at all above pleasure of shopping, bargaining, seeing and buying pretty things; gave herself little treat obedient to husband's orders; purchased quantity of lady's gear, showing great deal of taste and elegant discernment as all shopfolks said.
- **Attitude to War**: Not much alarmed about ensuing war; Bonaparty to be crushed almost without struggle. Held him in utter contempt; took her opinions from those surrounding her, being too humble-minded to think for itself. Acquitted herself with considerable liveliness and credit on her first appearance in genteel world of London.
- **Chatham Arrival - CURRENT**: Recognized friendly countenance of Captain Dobbin at inn door when Jos's fine carriage arrived. Found triangular billet on pink paper in sitting-room addressed to Mrs. Captain Osborne, sealed with dove and olive branch in light blue sealing wax, written in large undecided female hand—from Mrs. Major O'Dowd requesting her company that very evening to small friendly party.

**Rebecca Sharp (Mrs. Rebecca Rawdon Crawley)** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- **Miss Crawley Reconciliation - PERMANENTLY FAILED**: Successfully reconciled with Miss Briggs on beach. Initiated letter-writing campaign: Rawdon dictated (Rebecca composed) tender letter expressing humble acceptance of marriage, desire for reconciliation before departure. Miss Crawley recognized Rebecca's composition not Rawdon's (noting his letters full of bad spelling, dashes, bad grammar, money requests); concluded "that little serpent of a governess who rules him"; believed all relatives want her dead for money. Despite Briggs' reports of letter touching her, Miss Crawley remained unmoved.
- **Meeting with Rawdon and Miss Crawley - EXECUTED, DISAPPOINTING OUTCOME**: Rawdon met Miss Crawley on Cliff when she took air in chair; she held out couple of fingers with "smiling and good-humoured air." Rawdon turned red as scarlet with rapture and confusion. Miss Crawley subsequently remarked to Briggs: "Rawdon is getting very fat and old...His nose has become red, and he is exceedingly coarse in appearance. His marriage to that woman has hopelessly vulgarised him...he smelt of gin abominably."
- **Miss Crawley's Final Refusal**: Declined to receive Rebecca; instructed Briggs to write letter stating her health too delicate for family discussions; thanked Rawdon for coming; instructed him to call upon her lawyer in Gray's Inn Square. Letter's reference to lawyer provided Rawdon some consolation after disappointment.
- **Monetary Scheme - EXECUTED**: Sent crumpled family-note to Rawdon requesting money from "Cupid" (George) before departure; Rawdon extracted considerable payment from George in bank-notes and bill on agents. Rebecca remarked to Rawdon: "A comfortable inn in Brighton is better than a spunging-house in Chancery Lane"; noted Mr. Jos and Captain Cupid are better companions than sheriff's officers.
- **Debtor Evasion - EXECUTED**: Packed all chief valuables and sent them off under care of George's servant on coach back to London.
- **Current Status - LONDON**: Rebecca in London with furious Rawdon (outcome of Miss Crawley's lawyer communication negative). Status regarding General Tufto's staff unclear.

**John Osborne (Old Mr. Osborne)** [MAJOR CHARACTER - FINAL ACTION COMPLETED]
- Wealthy merchant; George's father; savage, determined man
- **Disinheritance - EXECUTED AND COMMUNICATED**: Upon learning George married Amelia, erupted in fury. Retreated to study; locked door; retrieved mahogany escritoire containing all George's documents since childhood; examined papers with "curses quivering on livid lips" and "horrid hatred and disappointment"; marked, docketed, catalogued with dates. Commissioned lawyer to draft letter stating determination "final and irrevocable." George ceases to be member of family; Money expended upon George in minority exceeds entitlement (£2,000 in 4 percent annuities); Mr. Osborne waives all claim upon George's estate. Letter delivered via Mr. Chopper to Dobbin.
- **Frederick Bullock Information**: Fred Bullock dines every day in Russell Square now; told old Osborne of George's appearance at lawyers—came in "bold as brass" and "drawn out every shilling." Osborne swore with great oath that he little cared when or how soon George spent it.

**Rawdon Crawley** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Secretly married to Rebecca; heavily indebted
- **Money Extraction - EXECUTED**: Sent crumpled family-note requesting money from George; extracted considerable payment in bank-notes and bill on agents; lost £140 to George at cards
- **Miss Crawley Meeting - COMPLETED, EMOTIONALLY MOVED BUT REJECTED**: Met Miss Crawley when she took air in chair; she held out couple of fingers; Rawdon turned red as scarlet with rapture and confusion. Miss Crawley subsequently disparaged his appearance, character, and drinking. Went to Gray's Inn Square to visit Miss Crawley's lawyer; "came back furious" to Rebecca in London
- **Current Status**: In London, furious after lawyer visit

## Critical Facts and Status

- **GEORGE-AMELIA MARRIAGE - CHATHAM PHASE ACTIVE**: Married late April; disinheritance "final and irrevocable"; Amelia's face cleared reading letter; idea of sharing poverty pleasant. Both determined to go to Belgium together. George obtained £2,000 cheque from solicitors; gloated over money at Hulker and Bullock bankers. Currently at Chatham inn preparing for departure. Amelia emotionally stabilized after Fulham visit; completed shopping for foreign tour with great taste and discernment. Received invitation to Mrs. Major O'Dowd's small friendly party that evening at Chatham.
- **REBECCA-MISS CRAWLEY RECONCILIATION - PERMANENTLY FAILED**: Letter campaign revealed as Rebecca's manipulation; Miss Crawley refused reconciliation; sent Rawdon to lawyer with negative outcome; disparaged Rawdon's appearance and habits; Rebecca now in London with furious Rawdon.
- **FINANCIAL CRISIS - ACUTE ONGOING**: George disinherited; must live on captain's pay and £100/year widow's allowance; obtained £2,000 cheque but hotel bills and card losses had drained purse; paid Amelia's shopping with cheques on agents. Fred Bullock reported George "drawn out every shilling"; Osborne swore he little cared. Rawdon and Rebecca evaded creditors; packed valuables sent to London.
- **MILITARY CRISIS - CAMPAIGN ACTIVATED**: Regiment ordered to Belgium; party at Chatham inn; Dobbin present in military dress (shells on frockcoat, crimson sash and sabre); Mrs. Major O'Dowd accompanying, going in command with her husband. Margate packets sailing daily to Brussels and Ghent; war viewed as fashionable tour; newspapers laughed at Corsican upstart; Amelia held Bonaparte in utter contempt.
- **DEPARTURES STATUS**: George-Amelia at Chatham inn with Jos and Dobbin; awaiting Mrs. Major O'Dowd's party invitation; preparing to embark for Belgium.
